sizePanel() no longer calls resize() unconditionally. resize() clears a doughnut's arc geometry and update('none') would not repaint it, which is why the doughnut measured 0 arcs whenever a dimension changed: 2 FAIL, then 5 FAIL as the harness grew stricter, now 0.

corrections_in_this_pass: Chart.js 4.4.1 getElementsAtEventForMode returned nothing for a real click on this page even when the element reported inRange true, so the built-in onClick never fired. Chart clicks are therefore resolved by this page's own test against the bar and arc geometry, which is deterministic. The built-in onClick was removed so there is only one path.
A chart drawn with responsive:true has no bar geometry until the browser's next animation frame, so a click immediately after a re-render missed. draw() now forces a synchronous update.

The applied-filter banner element would not update from its own function although the filter itself was set correctly; the 'showing: ...' line now lives in the rows-table line, which updates in the same pass, and the visible Clear filter control is in the drill bar.

The warehouse file carries no customer, and no reference we hold joins to its order numbers. So a delayed line cannot be attributed to a distributor. The who-is-waiting tab is a part-number overlap, clearly labelled as a warning rather than a traced document.
Invoice, Shipped and ETD are empty on all 2,102 rows, so this extract stops before dispatch and cannot show time underway.
Power BI will not close the shipment gap: it reads the same SAP, which records billing, not shipping.
Fill rate is missing for Denmark, Cyprus, Greece, UMI, Germany (ISD) and Benelux (IBX) at the latest month available; those distributors are named, not filled in.

The UTI weekly series covers weeks 2 to 40 of 2026 and is the only market with a continuous run. The tidy file holds the body-part lines at distributor level; the wider 1415-line trend file should be used for any market-total claim.
Back-order and days-of-stock values are the latest reported month per distributor, which for some is 2024 or 2025; the month is printed beside every value so a stale reading is visible.

Charts that are clickable: the warehouse waiting-time stacked bar, the status bars, the over-30-days status bar, the parts-family bar, the air-against-sea doughnut, and on the customer backlog tab the distributor bar, the oldest-order bar and the family bar. The earlier pass verified the tabs by loading a URL with a fragment (for example '...#wh'), which makes that panel visible at load, so its charts were built at full size and the screenshots looked right. Jerome opens the page plain and then clicks the tab, and a chart built while its panel is display:none has a zero-size canvas, so ten of the twelve charts on the page were blank for him. Opening by fragment is not the same path as clicking the tab, and that gap is what let this through. Screenshots must now be taken after clicking the tab, from a plain load.

A defect of my own found while testing: the new waiting-tab block was inserted after the render call in the page script, so it never ran on load and the tabs after it did not render either. Moved inside the render pass and re-tested.

FOURTH REPORT OF BLANK CHARTS, and the method was as much at fault as the code. Every earlier round tested one path, and each round a different path was still broken. From this pass there is a harness that drives every tab and every dropdown option and records each canvas, and it must show zero FAIL before anything is called done.
The parts tab had never honoured its own dimension: its charts were hard-wired to AIM family and sea/air. That is why a dimension change on that tab looked like nothing happened.

sizePanel() called resize() on every chart each time a panel was shown, and resize() clears a doughnut's arc geometry while update('none') does not repaint it. The doughnut was therefore blank with 0 arcs on every dimension change. This was introduced by this agent in the sixth pass and is the mechanical cause of the fourth report.
This harness first reported 6 FAILs that were its own fault: it set scale_max=1 for a doughnut and then required scale_max>1. Corrected before judging the page.
